title: Positive coordinate noise contraction
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space. For $0\leq\rho\leq1$ and $q\geq1$, the one-coordinate noise operator $N_{i,\rho}$ satisfies $\|N_{i,\rho}f\|_{q,P}\leq\|f\|_{q,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, $0\le\rho\le1$, $q\ge1$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\|N_{i,\rho}f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{q,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
